subject: Embeddings adapter retrofit: architecture & next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings adapter retrofit: architecture & next steps

Hi Emily — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can scope the demo/POC effectively: 

Key context you shared:
- Current provider: VectorCo (hosted), ~1536-dim vectors, using their managed index for nearest-neighbor lookups.
- Query profile: 90% short user queries (avg 32 tokens), 10% long contextual queries (up to 512 tokens).
- QPS today: baseline 8 qps with spikes to 35 qps during peak campaigns.
- Migration constraints: zero-downtime cutover preferred, need to preserve semantic similarity distribution across historical vectors.

Primary goals for POC:
1) Validate parity on relevance (top-5 rerank) vs VectorCo for 1536-dim embeddings.
2) Demonstrate batching + prefix caching to keep tail latency <120ms for short queries.
3) Show migration approach: dual-write -> background backfill -> cutover with rollback plan.

Suggested technical workstreams (we can refine after your internal sync):
- SDK + Auth: we'll provide a lightweight adapter (Node + Python) that plugs into your current ingestion pipeline. Auth via API keys with optional mTLS for the pilot.
- Vector sizing: test both 1024 and 1536 profiles (quantized where acceptable) to compare cost/latency/relevance.
- Batching/ingest: offline backfill via parallel workers (parallelism controlled by your DB/IO), real-time ingestion via small batches (8-16 vectors per request).
- Normalization: recommend L2 normalize embeddings before indexing; we'll include both raw and normalized evaluation metrics.
- Reranker: run a light-weight transformer reranker as a second-stage for top-50 candidates.

Attachments: please send a small sample of queries + documents (anonymized is fine). I attached a checklist template for the POC.

Next steps / asks:
- Emily: share a 500–1k row sample CSV of queries/doc pairs (anonymized) — we can use this for relevance evaluation.
- Storify: confirm whether you can enable a test service account with push access to your staging index (or allow us to set up a separate index we can populate).
- Redwood: we’ll put together a concise POC plan and propose a 3-week timeline (week 1: setup + dual-write, week 2: backfill + eval, week 3: cutover validation).

Available times for a 30-min technical kickoff next week: Thurs 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri 13:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — will loop in Aditya for the deep-dive on batching and normalization.

Best,

Thanks Nikhil — this is helpful and matches what we discussed. Couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Vector dimensions: yes, VectorCo uses 1536 today. We are open to testing a 1024 profile if we can get parity on top-5 accuracy. Cost is a factor — current vendor is fairly expensive on storage.
2) Normalization: we currently do no normalization on ingest — embeddings are whatever the model outputs.
3) Reranker: we already run a small in-house reranker for checkout recommendations but it’s slow; would like to evaluate Redwood's proposed light reranker.
4) Security/PCI: we cannot allow external services to call our production customer DB. Staging index is possible — I can provision a service account in staging with push-only rights.

I attached a 750-row anonymized sample (storify_sample_queries.csv). I’m copying Carlos (infra) to confirm staging account and timing.

Subject: Re: Embeddings adapter retrofit: architecture & next steps

Emily / Nikhil — quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff so we can optimize the agenda. I’ll cover runtime/kernel tradeoffs and batching during the call. Highlights: 

Vector dimension trade-offs:
- 1536: expect ~12–20% higher recall on some semantic tasks vs 1024; cost/latency increase roughly proportional to vector size.
- 1024: often sufficient for short-query ranking; consider mixed strategy — keep older historical vectors at 1024 quantized while keeping fresh writes at 1536 for sensitive signals. We'll run A/B evaluation to quantify delta.

Normalization + indexing:
- Recommend L2 normalization pre-index. This gives stable cosine similarity as dot-product; we'll evaluate both normalized and raw distances.
- For migration parity, we should export VectorCo's index stats (idf distribution & top-k overlap) — even small differences in tokenization/embedding postprocessing can shift top-k.

Batching and ingestion patterns:
- Ingest path: small real-time batches (8–16 vectors) for user-facing writes to maintain low per-request latency; larger parallel workers (64–256) for backfill. Tune based on IO throughput and cosine compute during backfill.
- For tail-latency control, implement prefix KV caching of rerank candidates for repeated queries (we'll show hit-rate samples).

Auth / SDK / routing:
- SDKs: we’ll provide Node + Python adapters with pluggable transport. Adapters will support: API key, short-lived JWT (recommended for staging), and optional mTLS.
- Routing: policy-based routing by region and latency SLO. For POC, a single-region staging routing policy is simplest; for production we recommend split by traffic class (interactive vs batch).

Reranker integration:
- Second-stage rerank as a synchronous call for top-50 candidates. We can optionally push reranker to asynchronous path with cached results for repeated queries.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a quick architecture diagram that maps proposed adapter placement and read/write flows. See attached architecture_diagram.png. Also attaching a short "auth_playbook.pdf" describing key rotation and service-account patterns.

Planned agenda for Thu 10:30 PT (30 min):

- 10 min: ingestion + batching + normalization plan (Aditya)
- 7 min: SDK/auth + routing (Karthik)
- 8 min: success metrics + next steps (Nikhil)

Action items before the call:

- Carlos: confirm whether you can accept a short-lived JWT approach for staging.
- Redwood (us): prepare the Node adapter and a small backfill runner that runs against the sample dataset.

See you Thu — I’ll screen-share the diagram.
